# Location Mapping

## Purpose
Turn a designed location into navigable camera geography: a floor plan with
cardinal orientation, named camera angles with approved plates, and sightline
data, so every shot can cite the nearest approved view of the set.

## Use When
- A location bible entry is approved and shots will be staged in it.
- Blocking or shot planning needs axes, sightlines, or angle references.
- A new scene demands coverage from angles the map does not yet include.

## Inputs
- `production/locations/<LOC_ID>/location.yaml` (landmarks, zones, adjacencies).
- Scene blocking needs from `production/scenes/*/scene.yaml`.
- Existing `production/locations/<LOC_ID>/map.yaml` and `refs/` plates.

## Process
1. Draw the floor plan: outline, zones, landmarks, entrances/exits, and a
   fixed cardinal orientation (declare which way is north and never rotate it).
2. Place practical light sources on the plan so lighting direction can be
   derived for any camera position.
3. Define named camera angles on a grid (`A1`, `B3`, `C2`…): position on plan,
   facing direction, approximate lens, and what landmarks the angle sees.
4. Cover the standard needs first — establishing wide, opposing over-shoulder
   pair positions, entrance-facing angle, and one clean background per axis side.
5. Generate or select a plate per angle, named `LOC_<NAME>_<ANGLE>_V##`
   (e.g. `LOC_STATION_C2_V02`), with a generation record each.
6. Record per-angle sightlines: visible zones, visible adjacent locations
   through openings, and which other angles it reverses against.
7. Register approved plates in `production/references/manifest.yaml`.
8. When blocking defines an axis, verify both sides of it have at least one
   mapped angle; add angles rather than letting shots freehand positions.

## Outputs
- `production/locations/<LOC_ID>/map.yaml` (`location-map.schema.json`).
- Angle plates in `production/locations/<LOC_ID>/refs/` and approved masters
  in `production/references/`.

## Quality Bar
- Cardinal orientation is fixed and consistent across plan, angles, and plates.
- Every angle states position, facing, lens, and visible landmarks.
- Reverse pairs exist for any axis a scene establishes in the location.
- Plates agree with each other — landmarks appear where the plan says they are.

## Common Failure Modes
- Plates generated independently per angle, each inventing its own geometry.
- No declared north, so screen direction cannot be audited later.
- Coverage only from one side of the likely axis, forcing crossed reverses.
- Angle names reused with different positions across versions.

## Related Agents
- production-designer
- shot-planner
- continuity-supervisor

## Related Commands
- /location-bible

## Notes
`reference-selection` picks the mapped angle nearest each shot's camera; a
sparse map silently degrades every reference plan in that location.
